newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of June 23, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - In a matter of months, a combination of streamlined PC manufacturing and fulfillment processes, fierce competition and dramatic processor price cuts will result in the most dramatic price reductions to hit the PC industry in years, PC Week reported June 23.

The fledgling Java operating system is proving to be more of a roadblock than a road to the network computer as problems with the three month-old operating system have trickled down to the product plans of NC vendors, such as Sun Microsystems' Computer Co and Wyse Technology, PC Week reported June 23.

COMPUTERWORLD - Sun Microsystems Inc this week will unfurl a plan designed to help banks and brokerages tie together all their financial services via a World Wide Web-based architecture, Computerworld reported June 23.

Midrange computer systems are just as vulnerable to Year 2000 problems as mainframe computers, but there are even fewer tools and skilled people to help fix them and some of the vendors who developed software for those systems no longer exist, Computerworld reported June 23.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Gateway 2000 Inc's deal to buy Advanced Logic Research Inc will give it instant access to high-end servers and a base of 5,000 value-added resellers, as part of its move to gain more of a foothold in the corporate marketplace, CRN reported June 23.

Price is the key reason why corporations buy products direct and service and support are the key reasons why they turn to the reseller channel, according to independent polls conducted by CRN and Information Week, CRN reported June 23.

INFOWORLD - A bug in Microsoft Corp's Internet Information Server 3.0 can give malicious hackers an opportunity to bring the Web software crashing down, InfoWorld reported June 23. The flaw was discovered by an Austin, Texas-based computer consultant and dupicated by an InfoWorld Test Center, as well as by Microsoft.

Looking to speed local-calling competition and the price cuts that it will bring, the Federal Communications Commission has ordered regional bell operating companies and large local exchange carriers to cut the rates they charge competitors that co-locate equipment in their central offices, InfoWorld reported June 23.

INFORMATION WEEK - Microsoft Corp is preparing its strongest challenge yet to Java when it formally introduces its next-generation Web browser, Internet Explorer 4.0, with its J/Direct technology that will provide a connection between Java and the Windows programming environment, Information Week reported June 23.

Compaq Computer Corp will deliver a line of DeskPro 2000 and 4000 desktop systems in mid-July armed with features and prices intended to do battle with its toughest competitor, Dell Computer Corp, Information Week reported June 23.

EE TIMES - Proponents of Apple Computer Inc's flagging Macintosh platform are preparing their own answer to Intel Corp's Merced CPU in the form of a 64-bit PowerPC microprocessor now in the works at the IBM-Motorola's Somerset Design Center, EE Times reported June 23.

SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV will crash the rapidly expanding low-end of the personal computer market this summer with a new X86 CPU and a multi-pronged product strategy, EE Times reported June 23.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - As DVD begins to take center stage, multimedia vendors are realizing that they must develop audio expertise or risk being left out of an emerging market, Electronic Buyers' News reported June 23.

Although some major original equipment manufacturers are publicly defending the health of the PC industry, soothing investors' concerns, more warning flags have gone up, indicating that business conditions may not be so rosy, EBN reported June 23.
